reasons.text: AIS off 110 min while radar still saw the hull over Cable A; it slowed to 2.7 kn meanwhile (6.0 kn before); 7 ships nearby kept transmitting, so not a coverage hole (cable-watch AIS-gap rule, as in the Yi Peng 3 case)
Under 5 kn within 1 km of Cable A for 36 min, average 2.4 kn (cable-watch slow-over-cable rule)
Speed fell from 11.6 to 3.2 kn for 1 h 58 min near Cable A, heading swinging up to 74°: the anchor-drag pattern seen in the Eagle S case
Lay alongside ALMA BAY at sea for 70 min, outside any port area (ship-to-ship transfer pattern)
Listed: Shadow-fleet watchlist (illustrative); owner Orion Grace Shipping Ltd (illustrative) on the Illustrative sanctions list (cable-watch watchlist rule)
AIS put it on land while radar saw it at sea 10.4 km away
AIS shows GNSS spoofing signatures: a position jump of 10.8 km in 2 min (implied 175 kn); positions traced a 9.1 km arc (360°) in 16 min
